page_title: NW.js (previously known as node-webkit) lets you call all Node.js modules directly from DOM and enables a new way of writing applications with all Web technologies.

summary.name: NW.js
summary.one_liner: NW.js (formerly node-webkit) is a framework for building desktop applications with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript that can call Node.js modules directly from the DOM.
use_cases: Building cross-platform desktop applications with web technologies
Packaging HTML5 and WebGL apps as native desktop programs
Using Node.js modules and APIs inside a browser-based UI
Protecting JavaScript source code in distributed desktop apps
summary.what_it_does: NW.js lets developers write native-style applications using HTML5, CSS3, WebGL and JavaScript. It provides full browser features alongside complete Node.js API support and access to third-party Node modules. Node.js modules can be called directly from the DOM and Web Workers. The page lists JavaScript source protection as a feature. The page shows Chromium 156 with Node 26.12.1 and version v0.119.2 with a SDK download option.
notable: Runs Node.js modules directly from the DOM and Web Workers
Combines Chromium browser features with full Node.js API support
